overall_summary: Bitcoin is reclaiming sixty-five thousand on the back of a US-Iran strike pause and crashing oil prices, while ETF inflows extend to a third straight week. Ether is outperforming and risk appetite looks supported by softer energy costs and steadier macro data. Upcoming Fed decision and lingering tariff and Red Sea risks keep some caution in the mix, but the near-term tone favors crypto.
key_points: ETF inflows hit third straight week
Oil plunges over 5%, easing risk pressure
Fed hold expected; tariffs and Houthis linger

items.title: Bitcoin Reclaims $65K as US-Iran Hold Fire, Oil Crashes
items.summary: Bitcoin pushed back above sixty-five thousand dollars after the US and Iran paused military strikes for a second straight day. Oil tumbled about five to seven percent on the news, easing inflation fears and sparking a risk-on move across equities and crypto. Ether led with gains over three percent while other majors advanced one to two percent. Traders should care because cheaper oil and de-escalation remove a major macro headwind right before the Fed decision, supporting the bounce off recent lows.
items.impact: Supports near-term risk appetite and could fuel a test of higher resistance if the pause holds

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Log Third Straight Weekly Inflows
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted about thirty-four million dollars in net inflows for the week ending July twenty-fourth, marking the third consecutive positive week. That came despite roughly four hundred sixty-five million in outflows over Thursday and Friday that ended a seven-day daily inflow streak, mostly from BlackRock's IBIT. After months of heavy redemptions earlier in the year, this repair phase shows institutional demand is returning, even if still cautious. Traders watch these flows closely as a leading indicator of spot demand that can stabilize or lift price.
items.impact: Modest positive demand signal that cushions downside and supports the July recovery narrative

items.title: Storj Files Chapter 11 Amid Wave of Crypto Failures
items.summary: Decentralized storage firm Storj Labs filed for Chapter Eleven bankruptcy to restructure legacy debts while pledging to keep the network running and even offering token holders equity in the reorganized company. The move caps a rough week that also saw BitMart and BitMEX announce orderly wind-downs plus Movement Labs seeking protection. Tokens like STORJ and BMX sold off hard on the news. This matters because it highlights capital flight toward AI and lingering stress in weaker crypto businesses, which can weigh on broader risk sentiment even if Bitcoin holds up.
items.impact: Negative for altcoin and sector sentiment, underscoring selective capital rotation away from crypto

items.title: CLARITY Act Faces Make-or-Break Two-Week Senate Window
items.summary: The Senate has roughly two weeks before its August recess to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, with a new draft merging prior versions and adding ethics language around officials and crypto. Negotiations continue on the ethics provisions amid Democratic pushback and some Republican concerns, while leadership signals the timeline is tight. Industry wants the market-structure rules badly for clearer SEC-CFTC lines. Traders should track any motion to proceed this week because passage odds and headlines can drive sharp volatility in Bitcoin and crypto stocks.
items.impact: Unresolved catalyst that could spark a relief rally on progress or disappointment sell-off if delayed

items.title: Bitcoin Options Traders Drop Hedges Ahead of Fed
items.summary: Bitcoin options markets have turned less defensive, with the put-call open interest ratio falling to about zero point five two from zero point seven six in late June. Short-term downside protection has cheapened sharply while traders pile into upside calls around seventy thousand. Implied volatility is subdued near-term even with the FOMC decision Wednesday. This positioning suggests the market expects a quiet outcome, but thin hedges mean any hawkish surprise or statement shift could amplify a move in either direction.
items.impact: Low near-term vol pricing leaves room for outsized reaction if Fed surprises

items.title: Ether Leads Gains as ETH/BTC Ratio Hits Multi-Month High
items.summary: Ether jumped more than three percent while Bitcoin rose about one percent, pushing the ether-bitcoin ratio to a three-month high near zero point zero three. The pair sits above its two-hundred-day moving average for the first time since January after gaining over twenty percent since early June. Analysts see this as a possible early sign of capital rotating into alts, though Bitcoin dominance remains elevated around fifty-eight to fifty-nine percent. Traders care because sustained ETH outperformance often precedes broader altcoin strength if risk appetite continues.
items.impact: Hints at potential altcoin rotation if the relative strength holds

items.title: US Durable Goods Orders Rebound 1.6% in June
items.summary: June durable goods orders jumped 1.6 percent, snapping back from May's 4.5 percent drop and matching forecasts. The core proxy for business investment, non-defense capital goods excluding aircraft, rose a solid 1.4 percent. This shows corporate spending remains resilient despite elevated rates, giving the Fed more cover to stay on hold and pushing back rate-cut hopes. Traders should watch yields and the dollar for the reaction, as stronger growth data supports the higher-for-longer narrative that can weigh on risk assets including crypto.
items.impact: Supports higher-for-longer rates, mixed for risk assets

items.title: Oil Plunges Over 5% on US-Iran Attack Pause
items.summary: Brent crude dropped more than 5 percent, briefly under 90 dollars, after the US and Iran paused military strikes over the weekend. WTI followed lower as hopes rose for de-escalation that could ease supply risks around the Strait of Hormuz. Lower energy prices ease inflation pressure and support risk appetite. Crypto traders should care because cheaper oil is disinflationary, potentially giving central banks more flexibility later while the immediate risk-on tone can lift Bitcoin and equities.

items.title: German Ifo Business Climate Rises to 86.6
items.summary: Germany's Ifo business climate index climbed to 86.6 in July from 85.7, beating expectations around 86. Expectations improved sharply while current conditions eased slightly. It suggests the eurozone's industrial gloom may be bottoming, offering the ECB a bit more breathing room. For global markets this is a modest positive for growth sentiment that can support European risk assets and the euro, with spillover to broader risk appetite.
items.impact: Modest lift to eurozone growth sentiment

items.title: FOMC Meeting This Week: Hold Expected Under Warsh
items.summary: The Federal Reserve meets July 28-29 with markets pricing a high chance of holding the funds rate at 3.5 to 3.75 percent. New Chair Kevin Warsh faces sticky inflation debates and recent oil volatility, with some earlier hike odds that have since cooled. The statement and any press conference will be key for the path ahead. Crypto traders watch closely because any hawkish tilt keeps liquidity tight, while a dovish surprise could spark a relief rally in Bitcoin.
items.impact: High-volatility event for rates and risk assets

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Near 4.68%, Dollar Steady Around 101
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 4.68 to 4.71 percent while the dollar index sits around 101.2 to 101.5. Stronger US data and the Fed blackout keep the higher-for-longer theme alive, though Middle East de-escalation and oil's drop have limited dollar upside. Bond auctions today will test demand. Elevated yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin, so any sharp move higher in rates can pressure crypto.
items.impact: Elevated yields a headwind for risk assets

items.title: Dallas Fed Manufacturing and Treasury Auctions Due Today
items.summary: Markets await the Dallas Fed manufacturing index later Monday, expected near flat or slightly negative, for another read on factory activity. The Treasury also auctions 2-year and 5-year notes, a key gauge of demand at current yield levels. Soft manufacturing would highlight uneven growth while a weak auction could push yields higher. These inputs feed directly into the growth-versus-rates debate that drives dollar, bond, and crypto positioning heading into the Fed.
items.impact: Secondary data and supply that can move yields

items.title: US and Iran Pause Mutual Strikes After Escalation
items.summary: The United States has paused airstrikes on Iran for a second or third straight night, with Iran reciprocating by halting its retaliatory attacks on regional US bases and allies. Top military advisors cited dwindling munitions stocks and limited targets as reasons for the halt, while diplomats push talks via Oman on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Netanyahu is set to visit the White House soon and may push for renewed pressure. Traders should watch this closely because sustained de-escalation would remove a major risk premium from oil and risk assets.
items.impact: Eases oil spike and geopolitical risk premium supporting risk-on assets

items.title: Oil Prices Ease Sharply on Iran Conflict Pause
items.summary: Brent crude fell several percent in early trading as markets reacted to the US-Iran strike pause, dropping from recent highs near or above one hundred dollars after weeks of Hormuz disruption and Houthi threats. Shipping remains constrained and the naval blockade continues, so the relief is fragile. Crypto traders care because lower energy prices cool inflation fears and support risk appetite after the conflict drove oil higher and weighed on growth assets.
items.impact: Reduces inflation pressure and supports broader risk assets including crypto

items.title: Ukraine Drones Black Out Towns Across Crimea
items.summary: Ukrainian drone and missile strikes have left whole towns in Russian-occupied Crimea without power or water, part of a sustained campaign hitting energy infrastructure, logistics, and shipping to pressure Moscow. Russian authorities have downplayed the crisis while Ukraine aims to make the war felt deeper in Russian-held territory. This matters for markets as it shows Ukraine's long-range capabilities remain potent and could prolong or intensify the conflict, keeping energy and grain volatility alive.
items.impact: Sustains war-related uncertainty and potential energy/grain disruptions

items.title: Houthis Escalate Red Sea Pressure on Saudi Shipping
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis have attacked or threatened Saudi oil tankers and claimed further missile and drone strikes, extending Middle East conflict risks to the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint after Hormuz disruptions. Trump previously vowed major punishment for Iran and the Houthis if attacks continue. Traders need to track this because dual chokepoint threats amplify oil supply fears even during a US-Iran pause and keep energy volatility elevated.
items.impact: Heightens dual-chokepoint oil supply risks and geopolitical premium

items.title: Pentagon Updates Show Over 600 US Iran War Casualties
items.summary: Updated Pentagon figures put US wounded in the Iran conflict above six hundred with around eighteen deaths, after earlier quiet revisions and questions over transparency on recent base attacks. The toll has climbed amid the recent escalation phase. This is relevant for markets as rising domestic political costs and midterm pressures could influence Trump's willingness to re-escalate or seek a deal, affecting risk sentiment.
items.impact: Raises domestic political risks that could shape future escalation or diplomacy

items.title: Trump Tariffs on 60 Partners Take Hold Over Forced Labor
items.summary: New US Section 301 tariffs of ten to twelve point five percent on goods from sixty economies, including the EU and China, took effect as prior temporary global tariffs expired, justified by forced labor enforcement shortfalls. Trading partners protested the rationale while noting some alignment with prior deals. Crypto and risk traders should note the inflationary and supply-chain drag potential even as markets focused more on Middle East events.
items.impact: Adds trade friction and potential inflation pressure on global growth
